summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships a WebRTC-signaled remote PTY agent
details: The package contains a single 12MB ARM64 Go ELF at bin/sxt with no source, no README, no hash manifest, and a package.json that declares only name/version/description/os/cpu/license. Symbol analysis of the binary shows it embeds the full pion WebRTC stack (webrtc/v4, dtls/v3, sctp, srtp, ice, turn/v5, stun, mdns, datachannel) together with coder/websocket for signaling and repeated pty/Control/Claude/C2 identifiers — the structural shape of a WebRTC-tunneled remote-shell agent that gives a remote peer PTY-level command execution on the host running the binary. The package follows the optionalDependencies platform-split naming pattern (sextant-cli-<os>-<arch>), so it is fetched and placed on linux/arm64 hosts of anyone installing the wrapper sextant-cli package; the license field in package.json links to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, and the package ships no documentation describing the tool's purpose or a legitimate operator-consent model for the remote PTY channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
